claims.text: POL-NS-21 makes the free wait run only 'from the driver's arrival at the pickup', and this category's own arrival test makes that arrival out only where the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace inside the STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m. It is not corroborated: EV-GPS-05064 reports arrival_check.corroborated = false with nearest_fix = null, and its admissibility notes record that the fixes either side of the hole are 'several hundred metres from the pickup'. I state that this artifact is impaired rather than clean, as POL-GEN-02(1) requires: EV-GPS-05064 carries weight_multiplier 0.6 and the issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION — a 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that straddles the 15:42:00 arrival marker, the entire waiting window and the 15:49:00 cancellation. The start of the free wait is therefore not established on this record, and the driver's cancellation is not shown to have been made 'after the free wait'.

POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD fee only 'when the driver cancels after the free wait'. Where the start of that wait — the driver's arrival at the pickup — is unproven, that precondition fails and the fee is not engaged. The driver is the filing party here (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER), and on the money record the 5.00 SGD has already gone back to the rider and been withheld from the driver (fee_reversed at 2026-09-06T19:30:00+08:00; payment_status REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 5.00). The driver's claim is not supported and the present state stands: NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03, which is party-relative and never restores a charge, leaving the disputed 5.00 where it already sits — with the rider.

If the Tribunal will not simply find the arrival unproven, POL-GEN-26 governs: 'when the driver arrived' is a fact POL-NS-21 needs, and the evidence that would carry it is impaired — the single trace of the driver's movement has a 720 s hole sitting exactly over the arrival marker and over the whole waiting window, leaving no fix within the arrival radius. POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated with the open question stated, and POL-NS-26 expressly subjects the finality of a no-show ruling to POL-GEN-26. ESCALATE is terminal and holds the amount rather than collecting it, so the rider continues not to carry the 5.00 SGD.

The parties' accounts conflict and nothing independent resolves it. The driver says he was at Blk 33 from 15:42; the rider says he stood at Blk 33 the whole time and never saw the car. The trace contains no rider track at all and no fix anywhere inside the 50 m arrival radius, so the one artifact that could settle presence is impaired at weight 0.6 with GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION. Whether the driver was in fact at the pickup is precisely the kind of fact POL-GEN-26 sends to a human reviewer rather than deciding on this record.

The only artifact capable of placing the driver at the pickup is EV-GPS-05064, at weight 0.6. Under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence in any finding that the driver was at the pickup cannot exceed that 0.6, and under POL-GEN-02(3) any ruling leaning on it must name it, its weight and its issue code. A DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling restoring the fee to the driver would have to rest on a fact this record cannot carry at full weight, and the impairment must not be airbrushed out of the reasoning.

I do not argue the contact obligation, because the record does not support it: the driver sent two in-app messages (15:42:20 and 15:46:00, both read) and placed one in-app call (15:45:10, unanswered, 25 s), all before the 15:49:00 cancellation, so POL-NS-23 is met and I do not contend otherwise. That concession does not carry the driver home: POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-21 are separate requirements, and discharging the duty to message and call says nothing about whether the driver was ever at the pickup — the point the impaired trace leaves open.

No traffic-data record was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05064-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, an absence that is itself citable but carries no fact. The record therefore offers no external explanation — congestion, diversion or otherwise — for the 12-minute hole in the driver's trace across the arrival marker and the waiting window.

claims.text: The driver's free wait is made out on the platform record alone: the trip record shows the driver marked arrival at 15:42:00 and cancelled at 15:49:00, 420 seconds later, so the cancellation came after the 300-second free wait POL-NS-21 requires and the driver was entitled to cancel this trip as a rider no-show.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is satisfied in full: the chat log carries two in-app messages sent by the driver (15:42:20 and 15:46:00) and the trip record carries an in-app call placed by the driver at 15:45:10, all three before the 15:49:00 cancellation. The clause requires a call to be placed, not answered, and this call rang for 25 seconds unanswered, which is the rider's doing, not the driver's omission.

The fee on the record is exactly the policy fee: EV-FARE-05064 shows 5.00 SGD charged and the derived money block reports fee_matches_policy true, policy_fee_sgd 5.00 and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd 5.00. Under POL-NS-22 the ruling that follows a no-show cancellation after the free wait is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 SGD fee.

POL-NS-24 has no application here. It governs a rider cancelling at no charge because the driver missed the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes; this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time at all, and the rider did not cancel — the driver did, for rider no-show, after the free wait had run. Nor can the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arise, because that credit requires the driver to have failed to attempt contact, and the driver both messaged twice and called.

I disclose that the GPS artifact is impaired: EV-GPS-05064 carries weight 0.6 with issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION, a single 720-second gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that swallows the arrival marker, the whole waiting window and the cancellation, and its derived arrival check reports corroborated false with no nearest fix. I do not present that trace as clean, and it neither confirms nor contradicts the arrival — a missing fix is not a fix showing the driver absent.

The fact POL-NS-21 needs — when the driver arrived — is established by a clean artifact independent of the impaired trace: EV-TRIP-05064 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and records the driver_arrived event at 15:42:00, the rider push notification 'Your driver has arrived' at 15:42:04 and the free-wait timer starting at 15:42:05, which is also the start point POL-NS-21 fixes the wait clock to. Because the arrival is carried by the compliant trip record, no fact the rule needs is left unestablishable on impaired or missing evidence, and POL-GEN-26 escalation is not triggered.

The rider's account has no electronic support while the driver's does. The GPS artifact contains no rider track at all — rider_track is empty — so nothing in the record places the rider at the pickup during the waiting window, and the chat log shows both driver messages were delivered and read by the rider (15:43:03 and 15:46:43) yet the rider never replied and never answered the 25-second call. A rider genuinely standing at the pickup who could not see the car would have answered or replied.

The disputed amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling is final at any confidence. Reading the outcome party-relative as POL-GEN-03 requires, NO_ACTION would simply leave the 5.00 SGD standing as refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver, which is a loss for the filing driver; the only outcome the record supports is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, which moves that sum back to the driver as compensation for the wait.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this case cannot be decided on the record, so it goes to a human reviewer and no money moves. The 5.00 SGD refunded to the rider on 2026-09-06 and withheld from the driver (fee_reversed at 19:30; payment_status REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 5.00) is held pending that review — it is not collected from the rider and not released to the driver.

Everything turns on one fact: whether the driver was at the pickup, so that the 300 s free wait of POL-NS-21 had begun before the 15:49:00 cancellation. This category's own arrival test (POL-NS-21) makes the driver 'at the pickup' only where the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. The only trace, EV-GPS-05064, is impaired: weight 0.6, issue code GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION — a single 720 s gap from 15:38:00 to 15:50:00 that covers the 15:42:00 arrival marker, the entire waiting window and the cancellation, with no fix inside the arrival radius (arrival_check.corroborated false, nearest_fix null; the fixes either side are several hundred metres away). Because the trace is impaired over exactly the stretch the arrival test reads, the arrival is undecided, and POL-GEN-26 sends a fact this record cannot establish — 'when the driver arrived' — to a human reviewer. POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on a no-show final, but expressly subject to POL-GEN-26.

The driver's case: EV-TRIP-05064 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and does record the 15:42:00 arrival button, the 15:42:04 rider notification and the 15:42:05 wait-timer start, and the 420 s from tap to cancel. But an arrival tap records only that the driver set it; the clause's own test for arrival is GPS corroboration, and no independent artifact supplies it, so the claim that the free wait is made out on the trip record alone, and the claim that only DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD can follow, are not accepted. The driver's other points are accepted: the POL-NS-23 contact obligation is met (two in-app messages at 15:42:20 and 15:46:00, both read, and a call at 15:45:10 ringing 25 s unanswered, all before the 15:49:00 cancellation, and the clause requires the call to be placed, not answered); POL-NS-24 has no application (on-demand trip with no scheduled time, and it was the driver who cancelled, not the rider); the fee on the record is exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes (fee_matches_policy true), so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises; and the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit cannot arise because contact was attempted. No POL-NS-25 repeat no-show flag arises either — the counter is absent from the profile and no fee stands.

The rider's case: the points that the arrival is not corroborated and that POL-GEN-26 governs are accepted, and the impairment is disclosed (EV-GPS-05064, weight 0.6, GPS_GAP_STRADDLING_CANCELLATION), which is the basis of this ruling. The rider's concession that the driver messaged twice and called once is noted; because POL-NS-23 is a requirement separate from POL-NS-21, discharging it does not show the driver was ever at the pickup.

Because the limb is undecided it supports neither the driver's compensation nor the rider's retention of the refund, so no monetary outcome issues and the disputed 5.00 SGD is held. Confidence is 0.6, the weight of the impaired trace on which this finding rests (POL-GEN-02(2)–(3)); the value in dispute is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so no higher confidence is required and this escalation rests on POL-GEN-26, not on any doubt about the value.

ruling.explanation:
This dispute is about the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-05064. The fee was charged to the rider at 15:49:04 on 2026-09-06 and then reversed at 19:30 — refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver — so the live question is whether the driver was entitled to that 5.00 SGD. The case cannot be decided on this record and goes to a human reviewer.

Why. The driver's case stands on the free-wait rule, POL-NS-21: a driver may cancel as a rider no-show only after waiting 5 minutes (300 s) from arriving at the pickup. The trip record (EV-TRIP-05064, weight 1.0) shows the arrival marker at 15:42:00 and the cancellation at 15:49:00, 420 seconds later, and the driver is right about that arithmetic. But POL-NS-21 requires both the trip record and the GPS trace, and this category's own arrival test makes the driver 'at the pickup' only when the trip record's arrival event is corroborated by the GPS trace within 50 m of the pickup.
